compute.note: parameters = np = iesm + iesd + iesh + (iback(1..4)) + iesfree + iessw + iesup + ieskin = 10 + 98 + 0 + 7 + 2 + 0 + 1 + 2 = 120 variational parameters (the code's own formula, Main_stripes_wf.f), matching the 120 optimised values listed in datprep.d after the namelists (Jastrow, backflow, pairing/field and chemical-potential terms, in the order the code reads them; &nelectrons nelup=132 neldo=156; one determinant of backflow orbitals per configuration). The script does NOT optimise: datasvmc.d sets itestr=2 ("VMC", measurement with the fixed parameters read from datprep.d; itestr=-2 is the minimiser) and the program README says the input files contain "the optimal variational parameters". The run it scripts is one measurement of ngen = 500000 Monte Carlo generations of nbra = 288 = N single-electron proposals each (one walker, nw=1), from which Energy.x takes bins of 1000 and drops the first 5. The &optimization namelist in the same file (nweight=5000 generations per SR step, ibinit=50, tau=0.02) is not read at itestr=2, and no file states how many optimisation steps produced the parameters, so samples and iterations (per optimisation step, and optimisation steps) are null. Doubt: the Fortran as committed is compiled for nx=48, L=288 (Main_stripes_wf.f parameter statement), so for this 288-site instance it matches. Searched for the optimisation run: the script, both input files, programs/vmc_hubbard (README, Main_*/Prep_* sources), the VarBench data file and Hubbard/supplements (Imada_group_overview.md, AFQMC.md), the VarBench paper (arXiv:2302.04919, Sec. S3 on VMC). No time is recorded anywhere.
